Every docs deployment since July has failed at the 'npx tsc' step of the
Vercel build: the deploy runs a fresh unpinned 'npm install', which now
resolves react-native 0.87, whose new function-component View ref types
make src/native-scan.tsx fail to compile. native-scan.tsx ships as raw
.tsx copied to dist (Metro compiles it) with a handwritten .d.ts — the
tsc output is never used — so exclude it from the compile set exactly
like native.tsx, react-native.tsx, preact.tsx, and angular.ts already
are. Verified against a clean-checkout reproduction of the Vercel build
(npm install --legacy-peer-deps → npx tsc → next build) on Node 22.

fix: honor configureBoneyard for transition/stagger/animate, fix fade, reserve skeleton height (#109, #110)

Three runtime fixes across all framework entry points:

- Prop defaults (stagger/transition = false, animate = 'pulse') made the
  prop ?? globalConfig ?? default chains unreachable, so these options were
  silently ignored when set via configureBoneyard() / boneyard.config.json.
  Defaults are now applied at the end of the chain only.

- The fade-out transition never interpolated: 'transitioning' was set in an
  effect after the overlay had already unmounted, so it remounted at
  opacity 0 with nothing to transition from. React/Preact/RN now derive it
  during render; Svelte uses $effect.pre. The overlay stays mounted through
  the commit where loading flips and fades from 1 → 0.

- The overlay gets pointer-events: none (an opacity-0 element still
  hit-tests, swallowing clicks meant for revealed content), and the
  container reserves the captured bones height via min-height while the
  skeleton shows — BoneSuspense renders {null} children, which previously
  collapsed the container to 0px and clipped the absolutely-positioned
  overlay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(extract): leaf tags recurse into block-level children (#112)

A tag on the leaf list (li, td, p, ...) is captured as one atomic bone only
while everything it holds is inline — a leaf tag wrapping block content (an
li around a card) is now walked into like any other container, so lists of
cards keep their inner structure instead of painting as solid slabs.

Merge pull request #108 from justinhnaylor/fix/ssr-stable-skeleton-uid

fix(react): derive skeleton uid from useId() instead of Math.random()

fix(react): derive skeleton uid from useId() instead of Math.random()

Math.random() runs during render, so the value differs between the
server and client pass. Under Next.js App Router with cacheComponents
(Partial Prerendering) this bails the static prerender: any route that
renders <Skeleton> emits an empty static shell and all of its markup is
deferred to request time.

useId() is stable across server and client renders. The result is
sanitized because uid is interpolated into CSS animation and @keyframes
identifiers, and useId() returns colon-wrapped values like ":r0:".

Verified with a single-variable production build: swapping only this
expression takes an affected route's prerendered shell from empty to
fully populated. bun test is unchanged at 146 pass / 11 fail (the
failures are pre-existing and environment-related).

fix(native-scan): resolve public instance before measuring on Fabric

BoneScan measured each host view via stateNode.measureLayout(). On the New
Architecture the host fiber's stateNode is the internal Instance, whose
measure methods live on canonical.publicInstance, so the call threw, was
swallowed by measureView's catch, and every bone was dropped — the scan
captured nothing with no error.

Resolve the public instance (Paper: stateNode already has the methods;
Fabric: stateNode.canonical.publicInstance) before measuring, and warn in
dev when the walk finds views but measures zero bones.

feat: add select option to pick breakpoint by container or viewport width

Bones are captured keyed by viewport width, but React/Preact/Angular select
the runtime breakpoint by the skeleton container's measured width. In
app-shell layouts where the container is narrower than the viewport, this
picks a smaller breakpoint than the one that produced the matching layout
(#92).

Add an opt-in select?: 'container' | 'viewport' prop + config option.
Default 'container' preserves current behavior; 'viewport' resolves against
window.innerWidth to match how captures are keyed. (Vue/Svelte already
select viewport-first.)

Addresses #92

fix(cli): preserve existing bones in --native scan registry

The native scan captures one mounted screen at a time. writeBones()
regenerated the registry from only the bones received during that session,
so re-running the scan (or opening a single screen) dropped every other
skeleton's import from registry.ts.

Seed the scan from existing .bones.json files on disk and merge them with
freshly-captured bones (fresh wins), mirroring the web/vite preservation
from #81. Also surfaces a clear message when a run receives nothing new but
keeps previously-captured skeletons.

Addresses #87 (registry overwrite)

fix(vite): resolve env[...] in auth config from .env files

The CLI resolves env[VAR_NAME] placeholders in auth cookie/header values
(gated on resolveEnvVars), but the vite plugin passed them through literally,
so cookies/headers ended up with the raw 'env[SESSION_TOKEN]' string and auth
failed silently.

- Load all (unprefixed) env vars from the project's .env files via Vite's
  loadEnv, with process.env fallback
- Resolve env[...] in cookie values and header values when resolveEnvVars is
  true, matching CLI semantics
- Warn when env[...] is present but resolveEnvVars is not enabled, and when a
  referenced var is missing

Fixes #84

fix(angular): inject @keyframes into document.head to survive ViewEncapsulation

Angular does not interpolate {{ uid }} inside inline <style> elements, and
emulated ViewEncapsulation rewrites @keyframes names with a _ngcontent-*
prefix. Both meant the keyframe name never matched the animation: reference
in getOverlayStyle()/getBoneStyle(), so shimmer/pulse/stagger animations were
completely static. This also affected the esbuild @angular/build:application
builder.

Move keyframes to a global <style> injected into document.head, built in TS
so the uid resolves and the name is unscoped. Cleaned up on destroy.

Fixes #95
Fixes #86

fix: HTTPS dev servers + preserve cross-run bones (fixes #80, #81)

#80 — CLI and Vite plugin now work against dev servers running over TLS:

- bin/cli.js: detectDevServer tries http:// on every port first, then
  falls back to https:// on every port. `probe` passes
  rejectUnauthorized: false when probing https so self-signed certs
  don't poison the probe.
- bin/cli.js: non-CDP browser context is created with
  ignoreHTTPSErrors: true so page.goto doesn't reject self-signed
  certs at navigation. CDP reuses the user's Chrome context so their
  existing cert handling applies there unchanged.
- src/vite.ts: ensureBrowser launches the non-CDP context with
  ignoreHTTPSErrors: true.
- src/vite.ts: configureServer / handleHotUpdate honour Vite's
  `server.https` config when constructing the capture URL — so a
  plugin running in an https dev server navigates to
  `https://localhost:<port>`, not `http://`.

#81 — previously-captured bones no longer drop out of the registry:

- bin/bone-merge.js: pure `mergePreservingExisting(collected, existing)`
  — kept as its own tiny module so it's unit-testable from src/ without
  spawning a real CLI. Fresh captures win; skeletons only in the
  existing set get preserved.
- bin/cli.js: merges `existingBones` into `collected` before registry
  regen unless --force is passed. Watch-mode recapture no longer wipes
  `collected` either — skeletons whose routes aren't re-visited stay
  put; fresh captures overwrite entries of the same name via
  capturePage.
- src/vite.ts: long-lived `knownBones` map seeded from
  `*.bones.json` files on first capture and updated in-place each run,
  so the regenerated registry includes bones whose routes weren't
  visited this pass. Fixes the cross-session drop-out that was
  especially bad after v1.8.0's single-page mode shipped.

fix(cli): treat URL with non-root path as single-page capture (fixes #78)

The CLI documents `npx boneyard-js build http://localhost:3000/dashboard`
as the way to capture a "Specific page"
(see apps/docs/src/app/cli/page.tsx). The implementation ignored that
contract: every URL was treated as a starting point, then expanded by
unconditionally following same-origin <a> links AND walking the
filesystem for additional Next.js routes AND adding any config.routes
entries. So passing /dashboard/analytics still scanned the whole project.

Now, when any URL passed on the command line has a non-root path:

- print "Specific page(s): N URL(s) — no link/filesystem crawl"
- visit exactly the URL(s) you passed; nothing else
- skip discoverLinks, discoverRoutes, config.routes, config.skeletons
- watch-mode recapture also stops following links out of the explicit URLs

Bare-origin URLs (`http://localhost:3000`) and the auto-detect path keep
the legacy crawl-everything behaviour. The check is in a tiny, pure
helper module so it can be unit-tested without spawning a real CLI.

- bin/url-helpers.js: hasNonRootPath / isSinglePageMode (pure JS so the
  CLI can import it directly without going through dist).
- src/cli-url.test.ts: 13 tests covering bare origins, root paths,
  multi-segment paths, query strings, https, malformed URLs, and the
  any-URL-has-a-path multi-URL case.

Smoke-tested both modes against an unreachable origin to confirm the
banner switches and the queue is correctly populated.

Merge PR #77: surface silent-stuck capture; honour config auth; reuse CDP context (#75)

fix(vite): surface why capture returns nothing; honour config auth; reuse CDP context

Addresses the silent-stuck case reported in #75: when the Vite plugin's
capture visits a route and comes back with zero skeletons, nothing is
written and nothing is logged, leaving users staring at
"watching for skeleton changes..." with no way to diagnose.

Changes:

- Per-route diagnostics: when `collected` is empty after visiting all
  routes, print each route's final path (so redirects are visible),
  document title, <data-boneyard> marker count, and any page.goto error.
  If every route has 0 markers, print a hint about registry wiring and
  auth redirects.
- Redirect warnings: log any route whose final path differs from the
  requested path at the first breakpoint (matches the CLI's behavior).
- Outer try/catch now logs all failures except the benign "Target closed"
  noise that fires on dev-server restarts. Stack traces included when
  debug is on.
- __BONEYARD_SNAPSHOT missing: previously the inner try/catch swallowed
  this silently. Now logged as a warning once per route.
- Per-skeleton snapshot throws: propagated as a visible warning with the
  skeleton name and error message instead of being eaten.

Plus two things that were silently broken for users with auth:

- boneyard.config.json is now read by the plugin. `routes`, `breakpoints`,
  `wait`, `out`, and `auth` (cookies/headers, sanitized against the same
  blocklist the CLI uses) are honoured as fallbacks; plugin options still
  win when both are set.
- `cdp:` now reuses the existing Chrome context via
  `browser.contexts()[0] ?? browser.newContext()`, matching the CLI fix
  in #73. Previously the plugin created a fresh context and threw away
  any logged-in session.

New `debug: true` option turns on verbose per-step logging
(route, breakpoint, marker count, launch/connect lifecycle).

fix(types): include boolean in AnyBone's JSON fallback

Container bones serialize with a trailing `true` as the 6th tuple element,
so a `*.bones.json` import with any container bone produces
`(number | boolean)[]` under structural JSON inference — which didn't
satisfy my previous `(number | string)[]` relaxation.

Widen to `(number | string | boolean)[]` to cover all three element types
that appear in the CLI's output.

fix(types): widen AnyBone to accept JSON-imported bones

When a project imports a `*.bones.json` emitted by `npx boneyard-js build`
under `resolveJsonModule: true`, TypeScript infers each bone as `number[]`
rather than a fixed-length tuple. The previous `AnyBone = Bone | CompactBone`
didn't accept that shape, so the auto-generated `registry.ts` failed to
typecheck:

    error TS2322: Type '{ ... bones: number[][]; ... }' is not assignable
    to type 'RegisteredBones'.

Forcing users to paper over this with `@ts-nocheck` or `as unknown as ...`
casts wasn't sustainable, and `declare module '*.bones.json'` is ignored
by tsc when `resolveJsonModule` is on.

Widen `AnyBone` to include `(number | string)[]` — the structural shape
of JSON-imported compact bones. `normalizeBone` already validates length
at runtime, so the relaxed static type is safe; a local `as CompactBone`
narrowing keeps the tuple-indexed assignment happy inside the function.

Also export `AnyBone` and `CompactBone` from the package entry so callers
annotating their own bones have the types available without reaching into
implementation-detail modules.

fix(cli): reuse existing browser context when connecting via --cdp

`chromium.connectOverCDP` returns a browser with the existing contexts
already loaded (cookies, auth, local storage). Calling `browser.newContext()`
on top creates a fresh, isolated context and discards all of that — which
breaks the `--cdp` promise documented in the CLI help:

    --cdp <port>  Connect to existing Chrome via debug port instead
                  of launching Playwright (reuses cookies, auth, state).

Reuse the default context when available, and only create a new one as a
fallback for a newly-launched Chrome with no context yet.

Before: hitting an authed route via --cdp redirects to sign-in.
After:  the attached tab inherits the user's existing session.

release: v1.7.8 — CLI --version, Windows route fix, explicit routes config

Bump to 1.7.8, changelog + banner. Packages three CLI improvements that already landed on main: --version flag (#64/#68), Windows path separator fix in route discovery (#65/#67), and explicit routes config (#66/#69).

feat(cli): support explicit routes in boneyard.config.json (#66)

Universal escape hatch for frameworks with lazy-loaded or unlinked routes (Angular loadChildren, auth-gated pages, custom routers). Users can list routes explicitly instead of relying on link-crawling + filesystem walking. Accepts plain paths or same-origin full URLs. Closes #66.

fix(cli): normalize path separators in filesystem route discovery (#65)

path.dirname / path.join return backslashes on Windows, breaking the group-stripping regex and string ops across all 5 framework branches in discoverRoutes(). Added toUrlPath() helper that normalizes separators before any regex runs. Fixes SvelteKit route groups never being stripped on Windows. Closes #65.

feat(cli): add --version / -v flag (#64)

Reads version from boneyard-js's own package.json via import.meta.url so it works regardless of install location. Closes #64.

release: v1.7.7 — Angular ng-content projection fix (#62)

Fix Angular <boneyard-skeleton> projecting zero bones during CLI capture (#62).

The template had two unselected <ng-content></ng-content> slots across a
*ngIf="buildMode; else runtimeMode" split. Angular only projects catch-all
content into one such slot; build mode rendered the empty one, so the
captured container was a 0×0 wrapper. Collapsed the template into a single
structure with one catch-all slot and moved runtime-only logic onto the
skeleton overlay. Added hasFixture detection in ngAfterContentInit so the
documented fixture+default sibling pattern doesn't double-render during
capture.

Also bumps boneyard-js to 1.7.7, updates the version banner, and adds a
changelog entry.

Packaged alongside the TS/JS registry filename detection from #60 that
landed on main earlier in this release cycle.

feat(cli): detect ts/js registry filename (#60)

Auto-detects whether the consumer project is TypeScript or JavaScript and
emits registry.ts or registry.js accordingly. Heuristics:

- tsconfig.json → ts
- jsconfig.json → js
- next-env.d.ts → ts
- typescript in dependencies/devDependencies → ts
- .ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts source under src/app/pages/components/lib → ts
- fallback → js

Both the CLI (bin/cli.js) and the Vite plugin (src/vite.ts) share a
single detection implementation in bin/registry-file.js; the Vite side
imports it through a thin .d.ts shim so tsconfig's rootDir stays intact.

Existing extensionless imports (import './bones/registry') are unaffected,

visible for a few frames.
